name: covering_point_is_chosen
why: The ordinary case: the last point that has already started.

name: exact_boundary_belongs_to_the_point_that_starts_there
why: A position equal to a point's start is inside it, not before it.

name: past_the_last_point_stays_on_the_last_point
why: Audio runs on past the final aligned sentence (credits, an outro).

name: before_the_first_point_resolves_to_the_first_point
why: Issue #200. Unaligned front matter, or a prologue the aligner dropped, leaves the listener earlier than any point. Both platforms used to answer 'chapter 0, sentence 0' / 'chapter 0, no preview' here, which is indistinguishable from a real hit on the opening sentence and let a re-map silently relocate a bookmark to the start of the book. The first point is the earliest place the map can actually name, and saying so explicitly is what makes the caller able to tell it apart.

name: before_the_first_point_when_the_first_point_is_the_book_start
why: The same rule where the first point genuinely is (0, 0) — the answer is identical, which is exactly why the old fallback hid the bug.

name: points_out_of_audio_order_are_sorted_first
why: Alignment emits reading order, which is usually but not contractually audio order.

name: zero_position_on_a_map_starting_at_zero
why: The commonest position of all must not be a special case.

name: no_points_at_all_resolves_to_nothing
why: A pair with no sync map has nothing to say. Each platform expresses 'no point' in its own shape — Python falls back to (0, 0), Kotlin returns null — but neither may claim a match.
